result.narrative:
Boeing is paying on time. The payment leg records 0 DPD with no open overdue notifications, and the only historical event on file is a single $650k invoice resolved 3 days late in June 2026, reported by one policyholder with no accumulation in the prior six-month window. TCI's $9M export line shows nothing owed. The negative signal is entirely in the news: a 9 November CNBC item reporting a 5% cut to the commercial airplane workforce as the production increase takes longer than expected, scored severity 4, base 80.0 decayed to 77.9 at 14 days old. Behind it sits a consistent 737 Max production and certification storyline from September to November - the late-2027 ramp-up deferral (38.0), the Max 10 certification delay (35.96) and the software glitch disclosure (35.83) - alongside neutral items including 57 September deliveries and an FAA finding that the software glitch is not a flight-safety issue.

The band is Watch at 27.3, from 0.65 x 0.0 (payment, 0 DPD) + 0.35 x 77.9 (news). The adjudicator agreed with caveats and the caveats matter here. The entire score comes from one article: with payment contributing 0.0, nothing else enters the formula, and the retrieved body of that article contains no text beyond the headline repeated - I confirmed this directly. The adjudicator also questions whether a 5% cut attributed to production timing supports a severity 4 mass-layoffs reading rather than an output and cost alignment story, and notes the 0.0 payment leg carrying 65% of the weight rests on a record the payment agent itself marks insufficient_history, last reviewed 2026-06-06 against news running to 2026-11-09. The three 737 Max items are correlated to one root cause, so they support Watch directionally but are not three independent confirmations.

The recommendation is MAINTAIN the TCI line at $9,000,000 for Tamrin Exports, unchanged, on the grounds that PD of 0.1727 sits within the 0.25 appetite target. Expected loss is 1,119,096 before and after, and maximum liability does not bind. Nothing in the payment record argues for a reduction, and the news that drives the band is not evidenced well enough to justify cutting exposure on it.

Two things would lift this. The score is 7.3 points above the Healthy line at 20.0, and because the news half-life is 365 days decay alone will be slow - so the faster route is manual confirmation of the 9 November report. If the underlying source shows a production-timing adjustment rather than distress, the severity 4 rating and with it the whole band should be revisited. A refreshed payment review confirming 0 DPD over the period in which the news cluster arose would also firm up the 65% of the score that is currently resting on thin, stale data.
